evidence.detail: The static parser resets one singleton state object, scans angle-bracket tags in the supplied String and recognizes exact 'align' and 'hov=' tag prefixes.
The state owns one rs/l/x$a enum field plus one integer field; exact reset clears the enum and sets the integer to -1, while the align tag assigns the enum's LEFT value.

The hov= parser consumes decimal/hex-like digits through the existing rs/l/h numeric helpers and stores the resulting integer without any second behavior. Its product meaning is intentionally left opaque.

A whole-JAR exact class-reference scan finds rs/l/x only in itself and its nested enum; no external exact-v308 consumer survives, so the name describes the self-contained rich-text alignment/state role only.

candidates.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for the isolated rich-text alignment/tag state parser. The opaque hov integer is not given a guessed domain meaning.

evidence.detail: The nested enum preserves exact source-level constant names LEFT, CENTER and RIGHT in v308 bytecode.
Its only exact owner is rs/l/x RichTextAlignmentState, which stores the enum as the parsed/current alignment state.
The enum contains no unrelated fields or behavior beyond ordinary values/valueOf plumbing.

candidates.note: Exact semantic enum identity from surviving LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT constants; the enclosing class name remains descriptive.
